trust_decision.summary: maxTake must bound the magnitude of the GraphQL `take` argument on every list findMany; the only enforcement is the `(take ?? Infinity) > maxTake` comparison in the shared findMany resolver, which checks only the positive direction, while maxTake itself is threaded in as the take argument's defaultValue by the schema builder.

landing_point.why: the advisory summary ('maxTake bypass with negative take') leads straight to the maxTake comparison; this is the only place maxTake is enforced anywhere in the tree

fix_sites.entry_point: GraphQL list query field (packages/core/src/lib/core/queries/index.ts:21-27) and nested to-many relationship field (packages/core/src/fields/types/relationship/index.ts:251-257 -> packages/core/src/lib/core/queries/output-field.ts:38-39); the same resolver is also reached by context.query.<List>.findMany (packages/core/src/lib/context/api.ts:24,47) and context.db.<List>.findMany (packages/core/src/lib/context/api.ts:79,92)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None - there is no separate O2 site and no O8 route; every route funnels into the one shared check in findMany, so a solver cannot argue any surface is out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Negative take is legitimate backwards pagination ('last N'): existing tests call findMany with take: -6 on lists without maxTake and expect the last 6 items. An over-broad fix that rejects any negative take, or clamps take to >= 0, breaks these routes; the published Math.abs comparison keeps negative take working up to maxTake.

O6_input_shapes: negative integer take of any magnitude (e.g. -5, -1000) - the bypass the fix closes
positive integer take (already enforced before the fix)
omitted take (argument default supplied by the schema builder equals the configured maxTake, or is absent when maxTake is unset)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second limit guard in the same resolver (e.g. a maxSkip magnitude check)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the resolver already owns the take guard and the limitsExceededError helper, so a maintainer adding another server-side limit would naturally put it beside this one; it would still be a one-line WHERE-type duplicate, not a new mechanism

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-relationship maximum on the relation list field's take argument
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the relationship field defines its own findMany arguments and its own GraphQL field, so a maintainer could believe the limit belongs on the field rather than in the shared resolver; it would divert to the same shared check anyway

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a server-side clamp of the admin pageSize/take value (pageSize comes from the admin URL at packages/core/src/admin-ui/components/Pagination.tsx:23-26 and is forwarded as take at packages/core/src/___internal-do-not-use-will-break-in-patch/admin-ui/pages/ListPage/index.tsx:219-220)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: maximumPageSize is already derived from maxTake here, so a maintainer could add sign handling at this producer instead of at the resolver; the request still ends up in the checked resolver, so this is also WHERE-type

O9_family: Improper input validation / numeric limit bypass through an incorrect comparison operator (CWE-20, CWE-480): maxTake is compared only against positive take, so a negative take of unbounded magnitude bypasses the server limit and can pull an unbounded result set.

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js 24 (CI, .github/actions/ci-setup/action.yml:10-14), pnpm 9.13.2 via corepack (package.json:10), preconstruct build, jest with esbuild-jest (package.json:59-75), Prisma 5.22.0 with the query engine library resolved from node_modules (tests/api-tests/test-runner.ts:34-38)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/api-tests/queries/limits.test.ts (describe 'graphql.maxTake'; the pinned tree has 'uses the default' and 'enforces the default', the fix adds the two negative-take cases) and tests/api-tests/queries/cursor-pagination.test.ts ('cursor pagination backwards', take: -6). Run with `DATABASE_URL=file:./test.db pnpm jest tests/api-tests/queries/limits.test.ts`; CI runs the api-tests on sqlite with no external service (.github/workflows/tests_ci.yml:79-93).

j.j_sites_touched: packages/core/src/lib/core/queries/resolvers.ts (one hunk; O1=2 because the root list query and the nested relationship field are two public surfaces, but both call this single findMany, so the check has to hold at only one site)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject or clamp negative take at the GraphQL layer (validation rule, argument definition, or a check in the root list query field) instead of making the existing comparison magnitude-aware; that breaks legitimate backwards cursor pagination and can leave the relationship/internal routes uncovered.
